reviewStatus: draft: needs review by a qualified coach or physio before release

steps: Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar, feet flat.
Grip just wider than shoulders; squeeze shoulder blades together and down.
Unrack, lower the bar to mid-chest with elbows about 45° from your body.
Press up and slightly back until arms are straight.
cues: Keep your glutes on the bench.
Use a spotter or safety arms near your limit.

steps: Set the bench to 30–45° and lie back, eyes under the bar.
Grip just wider than shoulders, shoulder blades pinched.
Lower the bar to your upper chest under control.
Press up over your shoulders.
cues: Don't let the bar drift toward your face.
Feet planted, back gently arched.

steps: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar about shoulder width.
Unrack with shoulder blades set.
Lower to your lower chest, elbows tucked close to your sides.
Press up by straightening the elbows.
cues: Hands no narrower than shoulder width protects the wrists.
Elbows stay tucked the whole rep.

steps: Set a flat bench so the bar meets your mid-chest.
Grip just wider than shoulders and rotate the bar off the hooks.
Lower to mid-chest with elbows about 45° out.
Press back up and re-hook at the end of the set.
cues: Set the safety stops just above chest height.
Keep shoulder blades pulled back.

steps: Sit with dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to chest height.
Palms forward or slightly turned in, shoulder blades pinched.
Press up until arms are straight, dumbbells over your chest.
Lower slowly until elbows are just below the bench.
cues: Control the bottom; don't bounce.
Bring the weights back to your thighs to finish.

steps: Set the bench to 30–45°, dumbbells on your thighs.
Lie back and bring the dumbbells to your upper chest.
Press up and slightly in over your shoulders.
Lower under control to the start.
cues: Wrists stacked over elbows.
Keep your back flat on the pad.

steps: Lie on the floor, knees bent, a dumbbell in each hand at chest height.
Upper arms on the floor at about 45° from your body.
Press up until arms are straight.
Lower until your upper arms touch the floor, pause, repeat.
cues: The floor limits range, which is kind to the shoulders.
Don't bounce the elbows off the floor.

steps: Lie on the floor, knees bent, kettlebell held at chest height, handle in your palm.
Upper arm on the floor about 45° from your body.
Press straight up, keeping the wrist straight.
Lower slowly until the upper arm touches the floor.
cues: Work one side at a time if you only have one bell.
Keep the bell resting on your forearm.

steps: Set both handles at chest height and stand in the middle, one foot forward.
Hold the handles at your chest, elbows back.
Press forward until arms are straight and hands meet.
Return slowly until hands are beside your chest.
cues: Lean slightly forward from the ankles.
Don't let the cables pull your shoulders forward.

steps: Set the pulleys at shoulder height and step forward, arms out wide.
Soft bend in the elbows, chest up.
Bring the handles together in a wide arc in front of your chest.
Open back out slowly until you feel a stretch.
cues: Keep the elbow bend fixed; it's a hug, not a press.
Stop the stretch before the shoulders strain.

steps: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells pressed over your chest, palms facing.
Soften the elbows slightly.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc.
Bring them back together over your chest.
cues: Go only as low as feels comfortable in the shoulders.
Use lighter weights than for pressing.

steps: Anchor the band at chest height behind you or wrap it around your back.
Hold the ends at your chest, elbows back.
Press forward until arms are straight.
Return slowly to your chest.
cues: Stagger your feet for balance.
Keep ribs down; don't arch.

steps: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, body straight from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor, elbows about 45° out.
Push the floor away to straighten your arms.
cues: Hips move with the chest, not before it.
Too hard? Use the incline version.

steps: Put your hands on a bench, box or counter, slightly wider than shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body is straight.
Lower your chest to the edge.
Push back up to straight arms.
cues: The higher the surface, the easier it gets.
Keep a straight line from head to heels.

steps: Feet on a bench or step, hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulders.
Body straight, core braced.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Push back up to straight arms.
cues: Shifts work toward the upper chest and shoulders.
Don't let the hips sag.

steps: Unrack the bar at collarbone height, grip just wider than shoulders.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to let it pass.
Lock out over your mid-foot, then lower to your collarbones.
cues: Don't lean back to finish the rep.
Elbows slightly in front of the bar at the start.

steps: Hold the bar at your collarbones, feet hip-width.
Dip a few inches by bending the knees, torso upright.
Drive up through the legs and press the bar overhead in one move.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders with control.
cues: The legs start it, the arms finish it.
Keep the dip short and straight down.

steps: Set a bench upright under the Smith bar.
Grip just wider than shoulders at collarbone height.
Press up until your arms are straight.
Lower back to your collarbones.
cues: Set safeties just above shoulder height.
Back flat against the pad.

steps: Sit on an upright bench, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Back against the pad, core braced.
Press up until arms are straight, dumbbells over your head.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
cues: Don't clang the weights together at the top.
Keep your ribs down.

steps: Stand tall, dumbbells at shoulder height, feet hip-width.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press both dumbbells straight up.
Lower under control to your shoulders.
cues: No leaning back.
Soft knees, strong trunk.

steps: Sit tall with dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you.
As you press up, rotate your palms to face forward.
Finish with arms straight overhead.
Reverse the rotation on the way down.
cues: Move smoothly; don't rush the turn.
Use lighter weight than a normal press.

steps: Kneel on one knee, the other foot in front, dumbbell at the shoulder on the kneeling side.
Squeeze the glute of the down leg and brace.
Press the dumbbell straight up.
Lower under control, finish the set, then switch sides.
cues: Keep your hips square and still.
Great for training one side at a time.

steps: Hold the kettlebell in the rack position: handle in your palm, bell on your forearm.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press straight up until your arm is straight, bicep by your ear.
Lower back to the rack position.
cues: Keep the wrist straight.
Don't lean away from the bell.

steps: Stand on the band with feet hip-width, ends at shoulder height.
Brace your core.
Press up until arms are straight.
Lower slowly to your shoulders.
cues: Widen your stance for more tension.
Keep ribs down.

steps: Start in a push-up position and walk your feet in, hips high like an upside-down V.
Hands shoulder-width, head between your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor.
Push back up.
cues: Your head goes in front of your hands, making a triangle.
Hips stay high the whole time.

steps: Feet on a bench or step, hands on the floor, hips high.
Head between your arms.
Lower the top of your head toward the floor.
Press back up.
cues: Harder than the floor pike; build up to it.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.

steps: Hold the bar with an overhand grip just wider than shoulders.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is about 45°, back flat, knees soft.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, elbows back.
Lower until your arms are straight.
cues: Keep your torso angle fixed; don't stand up.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.

steps: Bar on the floor, hinge until your back is nearly parallel to the floor.
Grip just wider than shoulders, back flat.
Pull the bar explosively to your lower chest.
Return it to the floor and reset each rep.
cues: Each rep starts from a dead stop.
Keep your back flat throughout.

steps: Put one knee and hand on a bench, other foot on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell with your free arm hanging straight down.
Pull the dumbbell to your hip, elbow close to your side.
Lower slowly until your arm is straight.
cues: Think elbow to back pocket.
Don't twist your torso to lift.

steps: Set a bench to about 30° and lie chest-down on it.
Let the dumbbells hang straight below your shoulders.
Row them up until your elbows pass your torso.
Lower slowly.
cues: The bench takes your lower back out of it.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.

steps: Hinge forward with a flat back, one hand on a bench or your knee.
Hold the kettlebell with the other arm hanging straight.
Row it to your hip.
Lower with control; switch sides after the set.
cues: Keep your shoulders level.
Pull with the back, not the biceps.

steps: Sit with feet on the platform, knees soft, holding the handle with straight arms.
Sit tall with your chest up.
Pull the handle to your belly, elbows close to your sides.
Let your arms straighten slowly.
cues: Don't rock back and forth.
Shoulders down, away from your ears.

steps: Lie under a bar or sturdy table edge set about waist height.
Grip it and hang with your body straight, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest up to the bar.
Lower until your arms are straight.
cues: Bend your knees to make it easier.
Keep your hips up in line with your body.

steps: Sit with legs straight and loop the band around your feet.
Hold the ends with straight arms, chest up.
Pull your hands to your belly, elbows back.
Return slowly.
cues: Sit tall; don't slump.
Pause and squeeze at the end.

steps: Loop a towel around the handles of a closed, locked door, or around a sturdy post.
Hold the ends and lean back with straight arms, feet close to the door.
Pull your chest toward your hands.
Lower slowly.
cues: Check the door is shut and locked toward you.
Walk your feet closer to make it harder.

steps: Set a rope at upper-chest height and hold it with palms facing down.
Step back until your arms are straight.
Pull the rope toward your face, hands splitting apart past your ears.
Return slowly.
cues: Elbows high, level with your hands.
Light weight, strict form.

steps: Anchor a band at head height and hold the ends.
Step back until there's tension.
Pull toward your face, hands going wide past your ears.
Return with control.
cues: Finish like a double-biceps pose.
Great for shoulder health.

steps: Hold a band in front of you at shoulder height, hands shoulder-width.
Arms straight, shoulders down.
Pull the band apart until it touches your chest.
Return slowly.
cues: Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Don't shrug.

steps: Hinge forward with a flat back, dumbbells hanging below your chest.
Soft bend in your elbows.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides.
Lower slowly.
cues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Light weights work best here.

steps: Lie face down on a mat or incline bench, arms overhead in a Y.
Thumbs up.
Lift your arms a few inches off the floor or pad.
Hold briefly, then lower.
cues: Keep your neck long and chin tucked.
Small movement; feel the upper back.

steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip just wider than shoulders.
Pull your shoulders down and brace your core.
Pull until your chin is over the bar.
Lower all the way to straight arms.
cues: Avoid swinging or kicking.
Use a band if you can't yet do full reps.

steps: Hang from the bar with palms facing you, hands shoulder-width.
Set your shoulders down.
Pull your chin over the bar.
Lower under control to a full hang.
cues: Usually easier than a pull-up.
Keep your legs still.

steps: Hang from parallel handles, palms facing each other.
Set your shoulders down.
Pull until your chin is above the handles.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Often the kindest grip for the shoulders.
Full range every rep.

steps: Loop a band over the bar and place a knee or foot in it.
Grip the bar just wider than shoulders.
Pull your chin over the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
cues: Use a lighter band as you get stronger.
Step out of the band carefully.

steps: Use a step or jump so your chin starts above the bar.
Hold the top with shoulders down.
Lower yourself as slowly as you can, 3–5 seconds.
Step back up and repeat.
cues: Builds strength toward your first pull-up.
Stop when you can't control the descent.

steps: Sit with thighs under the pad, grip the bar just wider than shoulders.
Lean back slightly, chest up.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, elbows down and back.
Let it rise slowly until arms are straight.
cues: Don't pull behind your neck.
Think of pulling your elbows into your pockets.

steps: Attach a close-grip handle and sit with thighs secured.
Chest up, slight lean back.
Pull the handle to your upper chest.
Return slowly to straight arms.
cues: Elbows stay close to your body.
Control the way up.

steps: Stand facing a high cable with a bar or rope, arms straight.
Hinge slightly forward, core braced.
Sweep the bar down to your thighs, keeping arms straight.
Return slowly to eye level.
cues: It's all lats; elbows stay nearly locked.
Don't bend over further to finish.

steps: Anchor a band high and kneel or sit facing it.
Hold the ends with arms up.
Pull your elbows down to your sides.
Return with control.
cues: Chest up, shoulders down.
Squeeze at the bottom.

steps: Lie across or along a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest with both hands.
Soft bend in the elbows.
Lower the dumbbell back over your head in an arc.
Pull it back over your chest.
cues: Only go as far back as feels comfortable.
Keep your ribs down.

steps: Set the bar on your upper back, not your neck, and step back from the rack.
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, brace your core.
Sit down and back until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.
cues: Knees track over your toes.
Use safety arms set just below your bottom position.

steps: Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders, elbows high.
Feet shoulder-width, core braced.
Squat down keeping your torso upright.
Stand up, leading with your elbows.
cues: If you drop the elbows, the bar rolls forward.
Cross-arm grip is fine if wrists are tight.

steps: Set a box or bench so your thighs are about parallel when seated.
Bar on your upper back, feet a little wider than shoulders.
Sit back onto the box under control, pause briefly.
Drive up to standing.
cues: Touch the box, don't crash onto it.
Stay tight while seated.

steps: Set the bar on your upper back with feet slightly in front of it.
Unrack by rotating the bar off the hooks.
Squat down until thighs are about parallel.
Stand back up.
cues: Set the safety stops first.
Feet forward lets you sit back.

steps: Sit with your back flat on the pad, feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Release the safety handles.
Lower the platform until knees are about 90°.
Press back up without locking your knees hard.
cues: Keep your lower back on the pad.
Re-engage the safeties at the end.

steps: Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest.
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Squat down between your knees, chest up.
Stand up through your whole foot.
cues: Elbows inside your knees at the bottom.
A great first squat to learn.

steps: Hold the kettlebell by the horns against your chest.
Feet shoulder-width, toes out a little.
Squat down, keeping your chest tall.
Stand back up.
cues: Push your knees out at the bottom.
Keep your heels down.

steps: Put your heels on a small plate or wedge.
Hold a weight at your chest.
Squat down deep with your torso upright.
Stand up.
cues: Puts more work on the quads.
Helps if your ankles are stiff.

steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width, arms forward for balance.
Sit down and back.
Go as low as you can with a flat back.
Stand back up.
cues: Knees follow your toes.
Keep your weight across the whole foot.

steps: Set up as for a normal squat, with or without weight.
Lower for a slow count of 3–4.
Pause briefly at the bottom.
Stand up at normal speed.
cues: Slow lowering makes light weights hard.
Stay tight during the pause.

steps: Stand in front of a sturdy chair, feet shoulder-width.
Sit back until you lightly touch the seat.
Stand straight back up without rocking.
Repeat.
cues: Great for learning depth safely.
Arms forward help with balance.

steps: Lean your back against a wall.
Slide down until your knees are about 90°.
Hold with your back flat on the wall.
Stand up to finish.
cues: Keep your knees over your ankles.
Breathe steadily.

steps: Take a wide stance, toes slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side and squat down on that leg.
Keep the other leg straight, toes up.
Push back to the middle and switch sides.
cues: Go only as deep as feels good.
Hold a doorframe if balance is tricky.

steps: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, feet hip-width.
Hinge down and grip just outside your legs; back flat, chest up.
Push the floor away and stand up, keeping the bar close.
Lower by pushing your hips back, then bend the knees.
cues: Never round your lower back.
The bar stays in contact with your legs.

steps: Hold the bar at your hips, feet hip-width, knees soft.
Push your hips back and slide the bar down your thighs.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, back flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand.
cues: It's a hip movement, not a squat.
The bar stays close to your legs.

steps: Sit with your upper back against a bench, bar over your hips on a pad.
Feet flat, about hip-width.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is level.
Lower with control.
cues: Chin tucked, ribs down at the top.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.

steps: Set a light bar on your upper back.
Soft knees, feet hip-width.
Push your hips back and lower your chest toward the floor, back flat.
Stand back up by driving the hips forward.
cues: Start very light.
Stop before your back starts to round.

steps: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Soft knees; push your hips back.
Lower the weights down your legs until you feel the hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes to stand.
cues: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs.
Neutral neck; look at the floor ahead.

steps: Hold a dumbbell in the opposite hand to your standing leg.
Hinge forward, letting your free leg rise behind you.
Lower until your body is nearly parallel, hips square.
Return to standing.
cues: Hold a wall for balance at first.
Keep your standing knee soft.

steps: Upper back on a bench, a dumbbell across your hips.
Feet flat, hip-width.
Lift your hips until your body is level.
Lower slowly.
cues: Push through your heels.
Pause at the top.

steps: Stand over the kettlebell, feet hip-width.
Hinge down and grab the handle, back flat.
Stand up tall, driving your hips forward.
Lower it back down by hinging.
cues: The best way to learn the hinge.
Shoulders stay over the bell at the start.

steps: Stand with the bell a foot in front of you, feet a little wider than hips.
Hike it back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to swing it to chest height.
Let it fall back and hinge to absorb it.
cues: The hips move the bell; the arms just hold on.
Learn the kettlebell deadlift first.

steps: Face away from a low cable with a rope between your legs.
Walk forward, feet hip-width, and hinge.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Hinge back slowly.
cues: Arms stay straight; they're just hooks.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.

steps: Anchor a band low behind you and hold it between your legs.
Step forward until there's tension.
Hinge back, then drive your hips forward to stand.
Repeat with control.
cues: Same pattern as the cable version.
Keep your back flat.

steps: Stand on one leg, knee soft.
Hinge forward, reaching your hands toward the floor as the other leg goes back.
Keep your hips level.
Return to standing.
cues: Hold a wall if you wobble.
Move slowly.

steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, hip-width.
Brace your core.
Lift your hips until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Lower slowly.
cues: Push through your heels.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.

steps: Lie on your back, one foot flat, the other leg straight or knee hugged.
Push through the planted heel to lift your hips.
Keep your hips level.
Lower and repeat; then switch.
cues: Don't let the hips drop on one side.
Pause at the top.

steps: Set the bar on your upper back and stand tall.
Step one foot back and lower until both knees are about 90°.
Push through the front foot to return.
Alternate legs or finish one side first.
cues: Keep your torso upright.
Use a lighter weight than your squat.

steps: Set the bar on your upper back in a split stance.
Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push up through the front foot.
Finish the set, then switch legs.
cues: Front knee tracks over the toes.
Set the safeties first.

steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Step one foot back and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front heel to stand.
Alternate legs.
cues: Easier on the knees than forward lunges.
Keep your chest up.

steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward and lower until both knees are about 90°.
Push up and bring the back foot forward into the next step.
Keep walking for the set.
cues: Take long enough steps that the front knee stays over the ankle.
Need a clear path of a few metres.

steps: Stand in front of a bench, rest the top of one foot on it behind you.
Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push up through the front foot.
cues: Find a stance where the front heel stays down.
Hard; start with bodyweight.

steps: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench, dumbbells at your sides.
Place one foot fully on the box.
Push through that foot to step up and stand tall.
Step down slowly and repeat.
cues: Don't push off the bottom foot.
Start with a knee-height box or lower.

steps: Hold a kettlebell at your chest, feet wide.
Sit into one hip, bending that knee, other leg straight.
Push back to the middle.
Alternate sides.
cues: Keep the bent knee over the toes.
Chest up throughout.

steps: Stand tall with hands on hips.
Step one foot back and lower the back knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front foot to stand.
Alternate legs.
cues: Keep your torso upright.
Gentle on the knees.

steps: Take a long split stance, back heel raised.
Lower straight down until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push up through the front foot.
Finish the set, then switch.
cues: Your feet stay put the whole set.
Hold a wall for balance if needed.

steps: Rest the top of your back foot on a bench or chair.
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push up through the front foot.
Switch legs after the set.
cues: Front heel stays down.
Go slow on the way down.

steps: Face a sturdy step, box or stair.
Place one foot fully on it.
Push through that foot to stand up tall.
Step down with control.
cues: Lead with the same leg for the whole set.
A lower step is easier.

steps: Stand with feet wide.
Shift into one hip, bending that knee, other leg straight.
Push back to the middle.
Alternate sides.
cues: Sit back into the hip.
Keep both feet flat.

steps: Pick up heavy dumbbells, one in each hand.
Stand tall, shoulders back and down.
Walk with short, steady steps for the set distance or time.
Set them down by hinging, not rounding.
cues: Don't let the weights swing.
Grip tight, breathe steadily.

steps: Pick up a kettlebell in each hand.
Stand tall with shoulders down.
Walk steadily for the set time or distance.
Put them down with a flat back.
cues: Keep your core braced.
Heavy but controlled.

steps: Hold one dumbbell in one hand, like a suitcase.
Stand tall without leaning.
Walk for the set distance.
Switch hands and repeat.
cues: Trains the side core.
Shoulders level the whole time.

steps: Hold a kettlebell in the rack position at your shoulder.
Stand tall and brace.
Walk steadily.
Switch sides after each round.
cues: Keep the wrist straight.
Don't lean away from the bell.

steps: Press a dumbbell overhead and lock your arm.
Brace your core, ribs down.
Walk slowly with the arm straight up.
Lower carefully and switch sides.
cues: Start light.
Stop if your shoulder feels unstable.

steps: Forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body is straight.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Hold for the set time.
cues: Don't let your hips sag or pike up.
Breathe normally.

steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder.
Stack your feet or stagger them.
Lift your hips so your body is straight.
Hold, then switch sides.
cues: Knees bent makes it easier.
Keep your hips pushed forward.

steps: Lie on your back, arms up, knees bent at 90° over your hips.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return and switch sides.
cues: The lower back stays flat throughout.
Go slow; breathe out as you extend.

steps: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Brace your core.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Return and switch sides.
cues: Keep your hips level, as if balancing a glass on your back.
Move slowly.

steps: Lie on your back and press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your shoulders and legs off the floor, arms by your ears.
Hold the banana shape.
Rest, then repeat.
cues: Bend your knees to make it easier.
Lower back never lifts.

steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, hands by your sides.
Curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Lower slowly.
Repeat without swinging.
cues: Small, controlled movement.
Breathe out as you curl.

steps: Lie on your back, hands lightly behind your head.
Lift your shoulders and bring one knee in as you rotate toward it.
Switch sides in a pedalling motion.
Keep it slow.
cues: Don't pull on your neck.
Rotate from the ribs, not the elbows.

steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms.
Brace your core.
Raise your knees toward your chest.
Lower slowly without swinging.
cues: Tilt your pelvis up at the top.
Use straps if your grip gives out first.

steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms.
Keep your legs straight and together.
Raise them to hip height or higher.
Lower slowly.
cues: Harder than knee raises; build up.
No swinging.

steps: Kneel facing a high cable with a rope by your head.
Hips stay still.
Crunch down, bringing your elbows toward your knees.
Return slowly.
cues: Round through the spine, not the hips.
Moderate weight, full control.

steps: Stand side-on to a cable at chest height, holding the handle at your chest.
Step out until there's tension, feet hip-width.
Press the handle straight out and hold.
Bring it back in; switch sides after the set.
cues: Resist the pull to twist.
Squeeze your glutes.

steps: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on to it.
Hold the band at your chest with both hands.
Press straight out and hold for a breath.
Return; switch sides after the set.
cues: Don't let the band rotate you.
Stand tall.

steps: Sit with knees bent, holding a kettlebell at your chest.
Lean back slightly with a straight back.
Rotate the bell to one side, then the other.
Keep the movement controlled.
cues: Feet on the floor makes it easier.
Turn your ribs, not just your arms.

steps: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders.
Lift your knees an inch off the floor.
Hold with a flat back.
Lower to rest.
cues: Keep your back flat like a table.
Breathe steadily.

steps: Stand holding a barbell with palms up, hands shoulder-width.
Elbows by your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: No swinging from the hips.
Squeeze at the top.

steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Keep your elbows by your sides.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Lower under control.
cues: Alternate arms or curl both.
Full range: straight arm at the bottom.

steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in.
Elbows fixed by your sides.
Curl up, keeping palms facing each other.
Lower slowly.
cues: Works the forearms too.
Keep your wrists straight.

steps: Sit back on a bench set to about 45°, arms hanging straight.
Palms forward.
Curl the dumbbells up without moving your upper arms.
Lower all the way down.
cues: Gives the biceps a long stretch.
Use lighter weights than standing.

steps: Stand facing a low cable with a straight bar or rope.
Elbows by your sides.
Curl the handle up to your shoulders.
Lower slowly.
cues: Constant tension through the whole rep.
Stand tall.

steps: Stand on the band with feet hip-width, holding the ends.
Elbows by your sides.
Curl your hands up to your shoulders.
Lower with control.
cues: Widen your stance for more tension.
Squeeze at the top.

steps: Face a high cable with a bar or rope, elbows by your sides.
Push the handle down until your arms are straight.
Pause briefly.
Let it rise until your forearms are just above parallel.
cues: Elbows stay pinned.
Stand tall, slight forward lean.

steps: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Keep your elbows pointing up.
Lower the weight behind your head.
Straighten your arms to lift it back.
cues: Ribs down; don't arch your back.
Go lighter if your shoulders feel pinched.

steps: Lie on a bench, dumbbells held straight up, palms facing.
Keep your upper arms still.
Bend your elbows to lower the weights beside your head.
Straighten your arms to lift.
cues: Move only at the elbows.
Control the lowering.

steps: Anchor a band high and hold the ends.
Elbows by your sides.
Push down until your arms are straight.
Return slowly.
cues: Keep your upper arms still.
Squeeze at the bottom.

steps: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside your hips.
Slide off, legs bent or straight.
Lower by bending your elbows to about 90°.
Press back up.
cues: Keep your back close to the bench.
Stop if the front of your shoulder hurts.

steps: Get into a push-up position with hands close together under your chest.
Body straight.
Lower your chest to your hands, elbows close to your sides.
Push back up.
cues: Do it from your knees to make it easier.
Hands can be a little wider if wrists complain.

steps: Stand holding light dumbbells at your sides.
Slight bend in the elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
cues: Lead with your elbows.
Light weight, no swinging.

steps: Stand side-on to a low cable, holding the handle with the far hand.
Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
Switch sides after the set.
cues: Keeps tension at the bottom of the rep.
Don't shrug.

steps: Stand on the band, holding the ends at your sides.
Raise your arms out to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
Repeat.
cues: Use a light band.
Shoulders stay down.

steps: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Raise one or both arms in front to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
Repeat.
cues: Light weight; no leaning back.
Stop at shoulder height.

steps: Make fists and place them on a mat, knuckles down, slightly wider than shoulders.
Body straight from head to heels.
Lower until your chest nears the floor.
Push back up.
cues: Keeps the wrists straight if bent wrists hurt.
Use a soft surface under your knuckles.

steps: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step, heels hanging off.
Hold something for balance.
Rise up as high as you can onto your toes.
Lower your heels below the step.
cues: Pause at the top and bottom.
Slow and full range.

steps: Stand on one foot on a step, heel hanging off.
Hold a wall for balance.
Rise up onto your toes.
Lower slowly; switch legs after the set.
cues: Harder than two feet.
Full range every rep.

steps: Hold a dumbbell in one or both hands, balls of your feet on a step.
Rise onto your toes.
Lower your heels below the step.
Repeat.
cues: Hold a support with a free hand.
Pause at the top.

steps: Stand under the Smith bar with the balls of your feet on a plate or step.
Unrack the bar on your upper back.
Rise onto your toes, then lower your heels.
Re-rack at the end.
cues: Set the safeties.
Slow lowering.

steps: Sit in the leg press with the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Legs straight but not locked hard.
Press the platform away by pointing your toes.
Let your heels come back slowly.
cues: Keep the safety handles engaged.
Don't bend your knees.

steps: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders.
Breathe in and let your belly drop, chest forward (cow).
Breathe out and round your back up, chin to chest (cat).
Flow slowly between the two.
cues: Move with your breath.
Stay in a pain-free range.

steps: Sit with one leg in front bent at 90° and the other to the side bent at 90°.
Sit tall.
Lean gently over the front leg.
Rotate your knees to switch sides.
cues: Use your hands behind you for support.
Easy, no forcing.

steps: Step into a long lunge, hands on the floor inside your front foot.
Drop your front elbow toward the floor.
Rotate and reach that arm up to the ceiling.
Step back and switch sides.
cues: Keep your back leg straight.
Slow and controlled.

steps: Lie on your side with knees bent, arms straight out in front.
Open your top arm up and over to the other side.
Follow your hand with your eyes.
Return and repeat; then switch sides.
cues: Keep your knees together.
Breathe out as you open.

steps: Kneel on one knee, the other foot in front.
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg.
Shift your hips gently forward until you feel a stretch.
Hold, then switch.
cues: Tuck your pelvis; don't arch.
Pad under the knee.

steps: Stand with feet a little wider than shoulders.
Squat down as low as is comfortable.
Hold, with elbows gently pushing your knees out.
Stand up slowly.
cues: Hold a doorframe if needed.
Heels on a plate help if ankles are stiff.

steps: Hold a light band wide in front of your hips.
Keeping arms straight, raise it over your head.
Continue behind you as far as is comfortable.
Bring it back over to the front.
cues: Widen your grip if it's tight.
Never force the shoulder.

steps: Kneel and sit your hips back toward your heels.
Reach your arms forward on the floor.
Rest your forehead down.
Breathe slowly and hold.
cues: Knees wide gives more room.
Relax your shoulders.

steps: Sit on a bench or lie on your back with one leg up.
Straighten the knee while pointing your toes up.
Bend it again while pointing your toes away.
Repeat smoothly; switch legs.
cues: A gentle nerve glide, not a stretch.
Keep it pain-free.

steps: Kneel facing a wall, front foot a few inches from it.
Keep your heel down.
Rock your knee forward toward the wall.
Return and repeat; switch sides.
cues: Knee tracks over the middle toes.
Move the foot back as you loosen up.

steps: Strap your feet in, grab the handle.
Push with the legs, then lean back, then pull the handle to your ribs.
Return: arms, then body, then knees.
Work hard for the interval, easy for the rest.
cues: Legs, body, arms; then reverse.
Damper around 4–6.

steps: Set the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom.
Warm up easy for a few minutes.
Ride hard for the work interval.
Pedal easy for the rest; repeat.
cues: Stay seated unless the plan says otherwise.
Hard should feel like 8 out of 10.

steps: Set the treadmill to a comfortable incline and pace.
Walk tall, arms swinging.
Keep a steady pace for the set time.
Lower the incline to cool down.
cues: Don't hold the rails.
You should be able to talk in short sentences.

steps: Walk at a pace where you breathe faster but can still talk.
Stand tall, arms swinging.
Keep going for the set time.
Slow down for the last few minutes.
cues: Comfortable shoes.
Outside or on a treadmill.

steps: Hold the handles at hip height, rope behind you.
Turn the rope with your wrists.
Hop lightly on the balls of your feet.
Work for the set time, rest, repeat.
cues: Small jumps, soft landings.
Low impact option: step over the rope.

steps: Stand, then squat and put your hands on the floor.
Jump or step your feet back into a plank.
Jump or step your feet back in.
Stand up or jump.
cues: Step instead of jump to make it easier.
Keep your back flat in the plank.

steps: Stand with feet together, arms by your sides.
Jump your feet out as your arms go overhead.
Jump back to the start.
Keep a steady rhythm.
cues: Step side to side for a low-impact version.
Land softly.

steps: Start in a plank with hands under shoulders.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Switch legs quickly.
Keep going for the set time.
cues: Hips stay level.
Slow it down to make it easier.

steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width.
Squat down a little.
Jump up explosively.
Land softly and go straight into the next rep.
cues: Land on the balls of your feet and sink in.
Skip if your knees are sore.

steps: On hands and knees, lift your knees an inch off the floor.
Move your opposite hand and foot forward together.
Crawl forward for the set distance.
Crawl back or rest.
cues: Keep your back flat and hips low.
Small steps.
